Multithreaded duplicated() and unique()

Source: R/par-duplicated.R
par_duplicated.Rd

  • par_duplicated() returns the same as base duplicated(), but much faster for large inputs. For a data frame, rows are compared, as in base.

  • par_unique() behaves like base unique() but is much faster for large inputs.

  • par_any_duplicated() behaves like base anyDuplicated(): it finds the position of the first duplicate (or 0 if there is none). It is much faster where the first duplicate comes late or not at all.

Usage

par_duplicated(
  x,
  incomparables = FALSE,
  fromLast = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_unique(
  x,
  incomparables = FALSE,
  fromLast = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_any_duplicated(
  x,
  incomparables = FALSE,
  fromLast = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

Arguments

x

A vector or data frame.

incomparables

Values that are never marked as duplicates, as in base duplicated(). FALSE means none; anything else goes to base.

fromLast

If TRUE, an element is a duplicate if an equal one comes later, rather than earlier.

nthreads

A whole number: the max number of threads to use. 0 means the RAYON_NUM_THREADS environment variable, or else all cores. The default is the parvenu.threads option, or 0 if that isn't set. Inputs too small to keep that many threads busy get fewer, and more threads than cores count as all cores.

Value

  • par_duplicated(): a logical vector as long as x (or with one element per row of a data frame): TRUE where an equal element (or row) comes earlier, or later if fromLast = TRUE.

  • par_unique(): x without those elements (or rows), as unique() returns it.

  • par_any_duplicated(): an integer, the position of the first TRUE of par_duplicated(), the last if fromLast = TRUE, or 0L.

Details

Computed in Rust when x has at least 1e4 elements (or rows) and is an integer, double, or string vector, a factor, a Date, or a POSIXct, or a data frame of such columns and logical ones. Anything else goes to base duplicated() unchanged.

Like par_match(), this hashes x in parallel. It marks the duplicates while it builds the hash table, so it never looks the elements up a second time, as par_match(x, x) != seq_along(x) would. par_unique() collects the first occurrences instead, so it never subsets x either.

Base anyDuplicated() stops at the first duplicate, so it is quick when one comes early. par_any_duplicated() checks the first 65536 elements (the last, with fromLast) that way. If none is there, it searches the whole vector.

Examples

x <- c(3, 1, 3, NA, 1, NA)
par_duplicated(x)
#> [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE
par_duplicated(x, fromLast = TRUE)
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE
par_unique(x)
#> [1]  3  1 NA
length(par_unique(x)) # number of distinct values
#> [1] 3
par_any_duplicated(x)
#> [1] 3

df <- data.frame(id = c(1, 2, 1), day = c("mon", "mon", "mon"))
par_duplicated(df)
#> [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE
